facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus is known from a partial skeleton found in the Early Cretaceous Xert Formation of Spain.
facts.quote: It is based on a partial skeleton from the Early Cretaceous Xert Formation of Spain.

facts.statement: The type species Tastavinsaurus sanzi was named in honor of the Rio Tastavins in Spain and paleontologist José Luis Sanz.
facts.quote: The type species is Tastavinsaurus sanzi, named in honor of the Rio Tastavins in Spain and Spanish paleontologist José Luis Sanz.

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus is classified as a sauropod dinosaur belonging to the clade Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Tastavinsaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur belonging to the Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: While originally described as a somphospondylan, Tastavinsaurus may actually be a member of the Brachiosauridae family.
facts.quote: Tastavinsaurus was originally described as a somphospondylan, but it may be a brachiosaurid.

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 120 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus sanzi has been estimated to reach a length of 16 meters (50 feet) and a weight of 8 tonnes.
facts.quote: The length of Tastavinsaurus sanzi has been estimated to be 16 metres (50 feet), and its weight has been estimated to be 8 tonnes.

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus had a proportionally short shin, with the tibia measuring only 55% of the femur's length.
facts.quote: The shin was proportionally shorter than in other sauropods, with the length of the tibia being only 55% of the length of the femur.

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus was a medium-sized herbivorous sauropod.
facts.quote: Tastavinsaurus era un herbívoro saurópodo de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: The left femur of Tastavinsaurus measures 131 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El muslo izquierdo tiene una longitud de 131 centímetros.

facts.statement: The pubis of Tastavinsaurus is straight and ends in a distinctive long, upward-curving pointed tip.
facts.quote: El pubis es recto. Termina en la parte inferior en una vista lateral convexa, un extremo áspero ovalado transversalmente ensanchado que termina al frente y hacia adentro en una llamativa punta larga que se curva hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The preserved portion of Tastavinsaurus's tail is longer than three meters.
facts.quote: La parte conservada de la cola tiene una longitud de más de tres metros.

facts.statement: The anterior chevron found between the third and fourth vertebrae has a Y-shaped profile ending in a plow-shaped blade.
facts.quote: El cheurón anterior encontrado, entre la tercera y cuarta vértebra, tiene un perfil en forma de Y, terminando en la parte inferior en una hoja en forma de arado.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Tastavinsaurus are opisthocoelous and relatively short.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la espalda son opistocoelas y relativamente cortas.

facts.statement: The anterior tail vertebrae of Tastavinsaurus are procoelous with flattened centra.
facts.quote: Las vértebras anteriores de la cola son procoelas y sus centros están aplanados.

facts.statement: The spinous processes in Tastavinsaurus are positioned forward on the vertebral arch and are low and mace-shaped at the tail base, a basic trait of Macronaria.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas están adelantadas en el arco vertebral y en la base de la cola bajas y en forma de maza, una característica básica de Macronaria.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tastavinsaurus belongs to the Somphospondyli or the Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Tastavinsaurus was originally described as a somphospondylan, but it may be a brachiosaurid.

facts.statement: The tibia is relatively short, measuring 56% of the femur length.
facts.quote: La tibia es relativamente corta con una longitud del 56% del fémur

facts.statement: In specimen CT-19, the first metatarsal bone is much narrower than usual.
facts.quote: El primer hueso metatarsiano en CT-19 es mucho más estrecho

facts.statement: The discovery was reported in scientific literature in 1999.
facts.quote: El hallazgo fue reportado en la literatura científica en 1999

facts.statement: The type species Tastavinsaurus sanzi was named and described in 2008 by José Ignacio Canudo Sanagustín, Rafael Royo-Torres, and Gloria Cuenca-Bescós.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Tastavinsaurus sanzi fue nombrada y descrita en 2008 por José Ignacio Canudo Sanagustín, Rafael Royo-Torres y Gloria Cuenca-Bescós

facts.statement: The holotype fossil MPZ-99/9 was found in a limestone layer of the Xert Formation dating to the Early Aptian.
facts.quote: El fósil holotipo, MPZ-99/9, fue encontrado en una capa caliza de la Formación Margas y Calizas de Xert que data del Aptiense inferior

facts.statement: It is one of the most complete sauropod skeletons known in Europe.
facts.quote: Es uno de los esqueletos de saurópodo más completos que se conocen en Europa

facts.statement: The holotype consists essentially of the posterior half, ten meters long, of a single individual.
facts.quote: Se compone esencialmente de la mitad posterior, de diez metros de largo, de un solo individuo

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tastavinsaurus is the sister taxon of the North American Venenosaurus within Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Tastavinsaurus es un taxón hermano del norteamericano Venenosaurus dentro de Titanosauriformes

facts.statement: This dinosaur provides information about non-brachiosaurid titanosauriformes during the Early Cretaceous in Europe.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio brinda información sobre los titanosauriformes no braquiosáuridos durante el Cretácico inferior en Europa

facts.statement: A 2011 analysis found Tastavinsaurus to be the sister species of Janenschia.
facts.quote: En 2011, un análisis encontró a Tastavinsaurus como la especie hermana de Janenschia

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Tastavins river, where Tastavin means "wine taster" in Catalan.
facts.quote: El nombre del género hace referencia al río Tastavins que a su vez dio nombre a Peñarroya de Tastavins. Tastavin significa "catador de vinos" en catalán

facts.statement: It is the best-preserved Early Cretaceous sauropod in Europe.
facts.quote: Es el saurópodo del Cretácico Inferior mejor conservado de Europa
